This article is spot-on, and I especially appreciate the nod to the recent article "The Coddling of the American Mind". The perceived notion that danger and pedophiles lurk at every corner is firmly embedded in many people's minds, along with the idea that everyone must be a winner in some form and unless everyone can be included, no one can. While the intentions behind these things are noble, the consequences are becoming painfully apparent. Equally as painful is the fact that many people I know were (and are) against such coddling, but are afraid to speak up for fear of being ridiculed or worse.

Pulling from my own childhood, my Mother was very much against this mindset when I was growing up. I was essentially booted out of the house most days (not in a bad way!), to go ride my bike or hike around in the woods playing make-believe. Now in my particular case I had the perceived "advantage" of living outside the city, but if you were to really think about it, the dangers above would in fact be replaced with the far more likely occurrence of a bear/cougar attack, falling into a ravine or being swept away by the nearby river. Childhood is fraught with "danger", no matter how you slice it, whether it's at home, at school or at play - and that's the way it's supposed to be! We are meant to learn from our mistakes, our failures, mishaps and awkward childhood social structure in order to prepare ourselves for the real world ahead.
